goalInOwnWords: Build a small factory line from scrap, fill each shift's order, and finish with more money than Sal the bot by placing parts well.
stoppedWhere: Results screen after finishing today's yard (17,382 dollars, 5 of 6 orders, Sal beat me by 282) and one 'try again from shift 6' that gave the same score; I sent the survey from there.
stoppedWhy: I hit my budget and I could not find the last 474 dollars in the try. I got close enough to want to come back, but I wanted to think about my layout first, not click through the same shift again.

stuck.what: Why an extra hopper feeding the old crusher changed nothing, and why the coach text said add a hopper when the furnace was the real limit; later, which of two slow machines a Tuner should touch.
stuck.gotOutHow: Used the live forecast number as a test bench: moved the part, watched the number, kept what raised it.

stuck.what: Could not make my spare splitters, docks and furnace useful; nothing told me how a spare splitter could help.
stuck.gotOutHow: Did not; left them on the shelf.

confused: The first lessons' big lit spots made it look like there was nothing for me to decide.
Sal's hint 'add a hopper' did not move the number; the furnace was the limit.
Coach text changed between 'short of scrap' and 'the furnace is the slow one' depending on where I held a part.
Splitters on the shelf with no obvious use after shift 3.
annoyed: Lessons dictate every drag and every spot, five lit spots in a row in lesson 2.
The Tuner only showed up late, at shift 6, when it would have helped most earlier.
Card offers were often only one that fit, so it felt like a vending machine, not a draft.
Hold-back note repeated 'the furnace again, 13 of 80 seconds' two shifts running with no clean fix on offer.
pleased: The forecast on every edit: 'this shift will pay X' lets me test a layout before running it.
The forecast was exactly right when the shift ran.
Skip to the end of the shift and 4x speed.
'What held you back' with real seconds.
Sal as a score to beat; ending one order and 282 dollars short made me want another go.
Moving a Tuner one cell was worth about 1,200 dollars.
bestMoment: Shift 3 of today's yard: I put a furnace in my second hopper's shard line and the forecast jumped from 1,296 to 2,196 before I even ran it, then the shift paid exactly that.
worstMoment: Lesson 2: five lit spots in a row, each with a sentence telling me what to drag, no choices at all.
oneChange: Let me skip or shorten the lit-up lessons for someone who knows factory games, put the Tuner in the offers earlier, and say plainly why a placement did nothing so my spare parts are not dead weight.
